content.text: {"decision":"accept_with_rework","confidence":0.85,"rationale":"The delivered consumer.py has two critical bugs: (1) run_once passes the raw return of queue.get() directly to handler, but get() returns a (receipt, message) tuple or None — the handler should receive only the message payload; (2) there is no call to queue.acknowledge(receipt) after successful processing, so messages accumulate in _unacked and the capacity bound is permanently consumed, eventually blocking all producers. The spec explicitly requires a receipt-based acknowledgement path that does not lose unacknowledged messages.","repair_plan":"Rewrite consumer.py so run_once unpacks the (receipt, message) tuple from get(), calls self._handler(message), then calls self._queue.acknowledge(receipt). Add try/except around the handler so that on failure we call self._queue.nack(receipt) to re-enqueue the message. Track processed messages as the actual message payloads (not tuples). Keep thread safety via the existing lock.","observed_artifact_sha256":"324762d15d114906ad55702613d14e7306b797922fafa03c5ab26d2d2d0d55e1"}
